paper_title: Minimum Cost Nowhere-Zero Flows and Cut-Balanced Orientations
classifications: Theory of computation → Approximation algorithms analysis
Theory of computation → Routing and network design problems
statement: We conclude with some interesting directions for future research. Firstly, is it possible to obtain a bicriteria approximation for min-cost well-balanced orientations? In particular, given an undirected graph 𝐺 = (𝑉, 𝐸), is it possible to construct an orientation 𝐸® such that (i) the cost of the orientation is at most a constant factor of a min-cost well-balanced orientation and (ii) the orientation 𝐸® is constant-approximately well-balanced, i.e., 𝜆 𝐸® (𝑢, 𝑣) ≥ ⌊𝜆 𝐸 (𝑢, 𝑣)/𝜌⌋ for some constant 𝜌? Secondly, can we improve on the (6, 6)-bicriteria approximation for WNZF(𝑘), on the (𝑘, 6)-bicriteria approximation for WCBO(𝑘), or on the 3-factor approximation for SWNZF(𝑘) for finite integer 𝑘 ≥ 6?
